Payments · quarterly runbook

Rotate the payments database credentials

Replace the primary and replica passwords without dropping a payment. Each step names who runs it and what to check before the next one starts.

Before the window

Book a thirty-minute window outside the payout batch, which starts at 02:00 UTC. Tell the on-call engineer for checkout, since a failed rotation shows up first as declined card payments.

Confirm access

The operator needs write access to the secrets vault and a shell on the bastion host. Check both a day ahead, while there is still time to request either.

Record the baseline

Note the connection count and the p95 query latency on the primary. The checks after each step compare against these two numbers.

Reading Where it is
Connection count The primary's overview dashboard
p95 query latency The checkout service's latency panel

Create the new credentials

Generate the new password in the vault rather than on a laptop, so it never leaves the vault in plain text. Add it to the database as a second valid password for the application role; the old one keeps working until the last step.

Run the role's login check against the primary and both replicas with the new password. All three must accept it before any service is told to use it.

Switch the services

Update the vault entry the services read, then restart them one region at a time, starting with the region that has the least traffic at this hour.

Checkout

Restart checkout's pods in batches of a third. Watch the declined payments graph after each batch; a sharp rise stops the rotation.

Ledger

The ledger holds long transactions, so drain each instance before its restart. A drained instance shows zero open transactions in its status page.

Verify

Every application connection should now authenticate with the new password. The database's authentication log shows which password each login used; filter it to the last fifteen minutes and confirm none used the old one.

Compare the connection count with the baseline. It should be back within twenty percent of it before you continue.

Retire the old password

Remove the old password from the application role, then from the vault's history. Keep the change ticket open for a day in case a batch job that runs only nightly still holds the old one.

The next morning After the nightly batch has run once on the new password. After a week After the weekly reconciliation job has run too.

Roll back

Until the old password is removed, rolling back is a vault change and a restart: point the vault entry at the old password and restart the services in the same order. After it is removed, create a new pair instead of trying to restore it.
